messages:
Marta: heads up — after HF->Redwood conversion of a candidate model, generation started spitting repeated <|unk|> tokens in chat mode. seems like special token ids moved around.
Jake: which special tokens are moving? bos/eos/pad/unk or some added_tokens ordering?
Marta: all of the above. quick dump shows BOS moved from id 2 to 5 and PAD swapped with UNK. reproduction steps below.
Marta: ```bash
# conversion we ran
python -m redwood_importer --from-hf ./hf/eleuther-small --out ./redwood/eleuther-small --quantize q4_0
``` 
Marta: then we inspected the tokenizer files and found the added tokens ended up appended in a different order:
Marta: ```json
{"added_tokens": [{"content":"<bos>", "id":5}, {"content":"<pad>", "id":2}]}
```
Priya: notable: HF's added_tokens.json usually doesn't contain explicit ids. If the importer calls `tokenizer.add_tokens()` after loading the base vocab, IDs will be assigned sequentially and can shift existing special token ids.
Jake: confirmed — our importer currently does `tokenizer.add_tokens(added_tokens)` without re-mapping special token fields. For HF to Redwood we then write out tokenizer.json with those new ids, but downstream code (chat templates, KV cache assumptions) expects canonical ids.
Marta: concrete symptom: chat template expects BOS=2. Prompt `<bos>Hello` produced weird prefix tokens and KV cache misalignments.
Sam: runtime log snippet:
```
WARN  [importer] special token id mismatch expected BOS=2 actual=5
ERROR [runtime] KV cache misaligned for seq 0 - dropping cache
```
Priya: two practical fixes:
  1) During import, if added_tokens are present, call `tokenizer.add_special_tokens(...)` for known names (bos_token, eos_token, pad_token, unk_token) rather than generic `add_tokens`. That preserves special token fields and avoids id-shifts.
  2) Alternatively, persist an explicit mapping file from HF names -> final ids and have the runtime remap the chat templates/kv keys on load.
Jake: also a note about quantization: we index embedding/LM head by token id post-conversion. If ids shift relative to the saved weights, generation will pull wrong embeddings — hence the garbage.
Marta: I pushed a small repro script to illustrate the mismatch and a debug harness to compare tokenizer.vocab, tokenizer.added_tokens and model.embeddings.weight indices.
Marta: repro snippet:
```py
# quick check
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('./redwood/eleuther-small')
print('bos id', t.bos_token_id)
print('pad id', t.pad_token_id)
print('added tokens', t.added_tokens)
```
Priya: I'll open a PR with an importer test: load HF repo, run importer, assert that the final special token ids match the HF config where possible and that a mapping file is produced when we cannot preserve ids.
Jake: small patch ready — importer will now prefer `add_special_tokens` for names present in config.json and will emit a `special_tokens_map.json` in the model dir listing canonical ids. Also added a CI job that runs the chat-template generation flow against a tiny sample to catch unk floods.
Marta: re-ran the conversion+quantize after the patch. Generation looks back to normal, KV warnings gone, and eval shows no regression vs float baseline.
Sam: great. can we add a short onboarding note for bringing new HF models: "do not rely on hardcoded special-token ids; importer may remap — use names or mapping file".
Marta: will add to docs and close the onboarding checklist item. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: checklist updated: importer-unit-test added, special_tokens_map output enabled, docs updated.
Jake: ack
Priya: ack
Marta: thanks all — I'll run a batch of other model bring-ups tomorrow to make sure this pattern doesn't recur.
